newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westfield America can spend US$350 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westfield America can spend US$350 mln.

text.p: Westfield Holdings Ltd chairman Frank Lowy said on Wednesday Westfield America Inc would spend up to US$350 million on buying shopping centres once it listed on the New York Stock Exchange in May.

"We see borrowings of maybe US$150-200 million (on top of US$210 million in equity) which gives us an opportunity to consider acquisitions of about US$350 million altogether," Lowy told a news conference.
Earlier on Wednesday Westfield announced that Westfield America Trust would list CenterMark Properties Inc on the New York Stock Exchange in May as Westfield America Inc and raise US$400 million.
It said Westfield America Inc would use the US$400 million proceeds to first buy Westfield Holdings Ltd's 50 percent interest in New Jersey's Garden State Plaza for US$145 million.
Westfield America Inc would then be granted an option to buy 9.8 million or 10 percent of Westfield Holdings shares for A$2 per share for a total A$19.6 million.
About US$210 million would be available for other acquisitions, including buying out existing partners in some Westfield America Inc properties.
Westfield America Trust's 67.2 percent holding in CenterMark would be watered down to about 50 percent after the float.
Lowy said many of Westfield America's partners were families or private companies who may want to sell down their stakes.
He said some of the shopping centres needed further development or redevelopment and the partners were unable to provide their share of the cash needed for the developments.
Some partners were also closed-end funds who had to sell up their holdings at a specified time.
Westfield America Inc would be the fourth largest listed shopping centre owner in the United States once listed.
